meta.description: Candidate PRIVATE grid infrastructure, parsed from the grid-connection language in DFFE REEA project titles. Each row is a renewable energy EA application whose own title describes a line, substation or connection. Feeds the question: which IPP-built assets are open to third parties?
meta.derived_from: nodal/reea_projects.json (DFFE REEA SHP+XLSX 2026 Q1), 2597 records, 170 matched
meta.method: Regex over the project NAME for line/substation/grid-connection language; voltage and asset type parsed from the same string. NOT a separate DFFE dataset - REEA is the RENEWABLE ENERGY application database and has no transmission technology category. Grid infrastructure appears only as part of a generation project description, which is why the parent extract shows nine tech values, all generation.
meta.CAUTION_1: AN EA IS NOT A BUILT ASSET. Status and decision date say what was authorised, not what exists. Cross-check against commissioning before treating any row as infrastructure.
meta.CAUTION_2: COORDINATES ARE THE GENERATION CENTROID, not the line. There is no route geometry here. Do not draw these as lines without a published route - see the Impofu and Koruson entries in transmission_lines.geojson for how routed and indicative cases are distinguished.
meta.CAUTION_3: shared_signal is a WEAK TEXTUAL HINT ONLY - the title contains a word like "common" or "cluster". It is NOT evidence the asset is open to third parties. The real test is spare capacity beyond the owner's own plant, or a stated intention to host others, and neither is in this data. Koruson qualifies on that test; Impofu does not, and NEITHER would be distinguishable from this file alone.
meta.next: NERSA transmission licences and developer statements are the sources that settle shared-vs-single. Ask Reapplication@dffe.gov.za whether grid infrastructure is ever published as a separate release.
